drug_authority.value: Licensed physicians may prescribe, administer, and dispense drugs including controlled substances for accepted therapeutic purposes. Opioid prescribing is subject to statutory limits (100 MME/day cap with exceptions for cancer, palliative care, end-of-life, hospice, and medication-assisted treatment). Long-term antibiotic therapy for Lyme disease is expressly authorized.
drug_authority.quote: prescribing or furnishing a drug, medicine, appliance, manipulation, method or a therapeutic agent whatsoever

license_status_types.quote: The board may issue a license limited to the practice of administrative medicine, or any other special license, as defined by routine technical rule of the board

foreign_medical_graduate_requirements.value: Graduates of unaccredited foreign medical schools must either be evaluated by the Educational Commission for Foreign Medical Graduates and receive a permanent ECFMG certificate, or achieve a passing score on the Visa Qualifying Examination or a substantially equivalent examination. Foreign graduates must also complete at least 36 months of ACGME-accredited postgraduate training. A waiver of postgraduate training requirements is available for foreign graduates (excluding Canada and Great Britain) who are licensed in another state and have at least 3 years of clinical experience, subject to board review of additional qualifications.
foreign_medical_graduate_requirements.quote: Graduate from an unaccredited medical school, be evaluated by the Educational Commission for Foreign Medical Graduates and receive a permanent certificate from the Educational Commission for Foreign Graduates

postgraduate_training_years_required.quote: Each applicant who has graduated from an accredited medical school on or after July 1, 2004 or an unaccredited medical school must have satisfactorily completed at least 36 months in a graduate educational program accredited by the Accreditation Council on Graduate Medical Education

pain_management_education_required.quote: By December 31, 2017, an individual licensed under this chapter must successfully complete 3 hours of continuing education every 2 years on the prescription of opioid medication as a condition of prescribing opioid medication.

opioid_prescribing_limits.value: May not prescribe more than 100 MME/day; no more than 30-day supply for chronic pain within a 30-day period (on or after January 1, 2017); no more than 7-day supply for acute pain within a 7-day period (on or after January 1, 2017). Exceptions for cancer treatment, palliative care, end-of-life/hospice care, medication-assisted treatment for substance use disorder, and emergency/inpatient/surgical settings.
opioid_prescribing_limits.quote: an individual licensed under this chapter and whose scope of practice includes prescribing opioid medication may not prescribe: A. To a patient any combination of opioid medication in an aggregate amount in excess of 100 morphine milligram equivalents of opioid medication per day

telehealth_prescribing_rules.value: A physician not licensed in Maine may provide consultative services through interstate telehealth to a Maine patient if registered with the board, fully licensed without restriction in the state from which services are provided, does not open an office or meet with patients in Maine, and provides only consultative services as requested by a Maine-licensed physician, APRN, or physician associate who retains ultimate authority over diagnosis, care and treatment.
telehealth_prescribing_rules.quote: A physician not licensed to practice medicine in this State may provide consultative services through interstate telehealth to a patient located in this State if the physician is registered in accordance with subsection 3.

physician_assistant_prescriptive_authori.value: Physician associates may prescribe and dispense prescription and legend drugs including schedule II-V controlled substances. Dispensing (other than professional samples) is limited to situations where a pharmacy service is not reasonably available, dispensing is in the best interests of the patient, or an emergency exists.
physician_assistant_prescriptive_authori.quote: "Prescription or legend drug" has the same meaning as "prescription drug" in section 13702‑A, subsection 30 and includes schedule II to schedule V drugs or other substances under the federal Controlled Substances Act
